events.title: Caesar Prevails at the Battle of Ruspina
events.description: In North Africa, Julius Caesar fought his former lieutenant Titus Labienus at Ruspina. Labienus was now fighting for the Republican cause. Caesar's forces were hard pressed, but the battle was an early step in his North African campaign during the civil war.
events.significance: The campaign that followed ended Republican resistance in Africa. That cleared the way for Caesar's dominance over the Roman world.

events.title: Charles I Storms the House of Commons
events.description: King Charles I of England entered Parliament with hundreds of armed men to arrest five members he accused of treason. The five had been warned and had already slipped away.
events.significance: The failed arrest badly damaged trust between the Crown and Parliament. It pushed England closer to the English Civil War.

events.title: Isaac Newton Is Born
events.description: Isaac Newton was born in Woolsthorpe, England. By the Julian calendar then used in England, his birthday was December 25, 1642. By today's Gregorian calendar it falls on January 4.
events.significance: Newton formulated the laws of motion and universal gravitation, and he helped invent calculus. His work laid the foundations of classical physics.

events.title: Burma Gains Independence
events.description: Burma, now called Myanmar, became an independent republic and left British rule. The transfer of sovereignty took place in the early hours of the morning in Rangoon.
events.significance: Burma's independence was part of the postwar decline of European colonial empires in Asia. Myanmar still marks January 4 as its Independence Day.

events.title: NASA's Spirit Rover Lands on Mars
events.description: Spirit, one of NASA's two Mars Exploration Rovers, touched down on the Martian surface. It landed in Gusev Crater after a months-long journey from Earth.
events.significance: Spirit operated far longer than its planned mission. It sent back evidence that ancient Mars had watery environments, which changed how scientists understand the planet's past.
